prompt: Cinematic wide shot in a data hall aisle: one hot-swap disk drive bay pulled halfway out of a rack server, its activity LED glowing warm amber. Cool blue rack-light from the right rakes across brushed steel rails and black polymer trays, the long rack row receding into deep shadow on the left. 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, graphite and steel blue with safety yellow cable accents, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos, extreme asymmetry with the drive bay off-centre right and generous negative space left.

rationale: The story is a decisive technical inflection point inside a real facility: a data hall where one disk bay represents the difference between a transcript and the machine state that matters. A cinematic still holds that single moment with atmospheric depth and material realism, avoiding sterile product-shot traps.
subject: a disk drive bay pulled halfway out of a rack server, activity LED glowing amber
core_thesis: What a crashed agent resumes from is the state its tools actually touched, not the transcript, so the runtime must sort turns by their OS effects and pay the write only where state changed.
core_conflict: chat-only recovery restores almost nothing on shell-heavy tasks, while full state saves every turn are 3.78x slower across many sandboxes sharing one host
composition: extreme asymmetry with the drive bay off-centre right and the rack row receding into darkness on the left
